issues.legal_issue: A sanad issued on the basis of an allotment does not preserve title after the underlying allotment is set aside.
material_facts: The appellant received a sanad after a managing officer allotted land to him.
A settlement authority later cancelled the allotment, and the appellant challenged that cancellation.
issues.conclusion: The appellant’s title based on the sanad fell when the allotment order was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied its decision in Shri Mithoo Shahani v. Union of India, [1964] 7 S.C.R. 103, that title founded on an allotment order cannot continue after that order is set aside.

predicates.allotment_cancellation_appeal: The proceeding challenges a decision cancelling an allotment.
predicates.sanad_based_on_allotment: An official issued a sanad to the claimant on the basis of the allotment.
predicates.underlying_allotment_set_aside: A competent authority set aside the allotment on which the sanad depended.

issues.definition: When an allotment-cancellation appeal concerns a sanad based on an allotment that has been set aside, the title founded on that sanad falls.

issues.legal_issue: Land that is within an urban area when allotted after the applicable rules take effect cannot validly be allotted under the governing definition of urban area.
material_facts: The allotment was made after the rules came into force.
The allotted plots had been included within municipal limits before the allotment was made.
The settlement authority cancelled the allotment because the plots were in an urban area.
issues.conclusion: The plots were urban land on the date of allotment, so the allotment was invalid under the main part of the definition; the proviso for allotments already made did not apply.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 2(h) of the Displaced Persons Compensation and Rehabilitation Rules, 1955 defined an urban area to include land within municipal limits. Its proviso addressed qualifying quasi-permanent allotments already made before the rules came into force, and did not govern a later allotment. The rules were made under section 40 of the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1954.

predicates.allotment_validity_case: The proceeding challenges whether an allotment was legally valid.
predicates.allotment_after_rule_commencement: The managing officer made the allotment after the applicable rules had taken effect.
predicates.land_urban_when_allotted: The allotted land was within an area treated as urban when the allotment was made.

issues.definition: In a proceeding about an allotment’s validity, a post-commencement allotment of land that was urban when allotted is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: A rule is not unconstitutional merely because it operates prospectively and thereby treats past and future allotments differently.
material_facts: The appellant challenged the definition of urban area as discriminatory under Article 14.
The rule applied to allotments made after it took effect, while its proviso addressed certain allotments already made.
The appellant’s allotment was made after the rule took effect.
issues.conclusion: The Article 14 challenge failed because the difference created by the rule’s prospective operation did not, by itself, make the rule unconstitutional.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that every law must have a time from which it operates and that a rule within the rule-making power is not invalid merely because it changes the law prospectively. It distinguished a possible challenge based on retrospective operation from a claim that prospective operation alone is discriminatory under Article 14. The rule was made under section 40 of the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1954; the appellant did not dispute that the rules were competently made.

predicates.equality_challenge_to_rule: A party challenges a rule as discriminatory in a proceeding concerning its application.
predicates.rule_operates_prospectively: The rule applies to events occurring after it takes effect rather than changing the legal consequences of completed past events.
predicates.alleged_discrimination_is_only_temporal_: The asserted difference in treatment rests only on the rule drawing a line between events before and after its commencement.

issues.definition: A rule challenged on equality grounds is not invalid merely because it operates prospectively and the claimed discrimination is only the resulting temporal distinction.
